topic: Arduino programming model: digital input and output
title: A button that lights an LED
instructions:
## Input in, output out

A push button is wired to pin 2 (it reads HIGH while pressed) and an LED to pin 9. During the simulated run the button is pressed twice, as shown under the board.

## Do this

Make the LED light **while** the button is held and go off when it is released. Read the pin with `digitalRead(2)` in `loop()`, and keep the loop quick (a `delay(20)` is fine) so the sketch notices every press.
hints: if (pressed == HIGH) digitalWrite(9, HIGH); else digitalWrite(9, LOW);
Or in one line: digitalWrite(9, digitalRead(2));
realityNote: A real button needs a pull-down resistor (or INPUT_PULLUP with the logic inverted) so the pin does not float, and it bounces for a few milliseconds on each press, which matters as soon as you count presses.
